main_text.p: multò certius sua fata, sibi à Deo im-pendētia;agnoscere potuit. Ita in sa-cra cœna,vbi ad res visibiles memo-randarum rerū nomina accesserunt, nihil iam ad perfectissimam commemo-rationē requiri videtur amplius. Dum enim visus noster cernit panē & vinum ,& aures audiunt nomina corporis & sanguinis Christi: sugge-ritur fideli menti,tum, ad quid nobis in cœna Domini panis & vinum co-ducant: tum, quid corpus & sanguis Christi nobis ad vitam, maximè æter-nam,conferant. Siquidè ista mutuā quasi operam sibi inuicem declaran-dis præstant, ut corporis & sanguinis Christi vocabula indicent quò panis & vinum referantur & respiciant: ac vicissim panis & vinum ostendant, corpus Christi pro nobis traditum, esurientibus iustitiam, esse panem il-lum vitæ de cœlo,qui dat vitam mun-do: sanguinem Christi pro nobis in remissionem peccatorum effusum, esse potum illum cælestem, quem sitien-

page.notes: Long s is rendered as plain s throughout, so the scan's "fugge", "fanguis" and "fibi" read as "sugge", "sanguis" and "sibi". "Siquidè" and "mutuā" are the least certain forms of the accents. The first line begins mid-sentence and the last word is hyphenated across the page break, so the paragraph is marked cont="true" and ends with "sitien-".
